news.title: Uefa, Concacaf and AFC push for Infantino to quit and discuss rival competitions
news.lede: Confederations write open letter damning Fifa president. Concacaf president Montagliani seen as top contender. Uefa, the Asian Football Confederation and Concacaf will push for Gianni Infantino to resign after writing an open letter calling for “leadership that serves football, not seeks to command it”. In a dramatic escalation of the war that has threatened to tear football apart since details emerged of the Fifa president’s failed Football Forward Enterprise (FFE) scheme, the three governing bodies accused Infantino of “trust broken through deception” and condemned his failure to acknowledge that the proposal should not have been unilaterally launched.

news.title: Training Report: Bayern Munich injured stars almost ready; World Cup contingent out a little longer; and MORE!
news.lede: It has been a busy few days for Bayern Munich when it comes to personnel news. News that emerged on Sunday from Säbener Straße indicated that Bayern Munich stars Alphonso Davies and Jamal Musiala could be back in team training this week (per Bild via @iMiaSanMia): > Among the players currently recovering from injury, Alphonso Davies and Jamal Musiala are the most advanced in their rehab. Both are expected back in team training at the beginning of the coming week [@BILD] In addition, Bild (via @iMiaSanMia) is reporting that Harry Kane, Michael Olise and Dayot Upamecano are getting more time off and will not be fully back in action until next week: > Harry Kane, Michael Olise and Dayot Upamecano have been given more vacation time and won’t return to Munich until the end of the coming week.

news.title: World Cup co-hosts US, Canada oppose Infantino
news.lede: Fifa president Gianni Infantino has come under intense pressure since first proposing and then shelving a plan to raise private investment for a new commercial subsidiary. (AFP pic) LOS ANGELES: The football federations of the US and Canada - two of the 2026 World Cup host nations - on Monday backed a statement from three confederations criticising Fifa president Gianni Infantino. US Soccer, Canada Soccer, Caribbean Football Union (the CFU) and Central American Football Union (UNCAF) said they "stand together, along with our colleagues around the world, in calling for meaningful change that strengthens Fifa's governance, transparency and accountability". That puts the US and Canada at odds with the third co-host of this year's World Cup, Mexico, which has given Infantino its backing.

news.title: Rebel World Cup? Shock new FIFA threat emerges as brutal letter escalates civil war
news.lede: Football’s ongoing civil war has escalated further, with FIFA and embattled president Gianni Infantino facing the threat of breakaway competitions in response to the aborted plan to sell a stake in the World Cup. UEFA, the Asian Football Confederation and CONCACAF, which represents North and Central America and the Caribbean, have banded together to issue a savage open letter accusing Infantino and the world governing body of “deception” and abandoning their duty to the game. With UEFA still threatening a boycott of future World Cups, reports have emerged that the three bodies are in discussions over the possibility of setting up a separate tournament to allow players the opportunity to compete in major competition should FIFA not acquiesce to a series of demands. news.title: Germany’s Jonathan Tah on his missed World Cup penalty
news.lede: Jonathan Tah stepped up to take the pivotal penalty in Germany’s World Cup shootout loss to Paraguay, but it went all went awry — in fact, it went absolute chimneys. But the Bayern Munich defender has taken it all in stride. “My general approach is to prepare myself for situations like that,” Tah relayed in an interview with Sky Germany’s Torben Hoffmann (as captured by @iMiaSanMia). “In life, you’re always going to experience difficult moments and setbacks.

news.title: Somali referee Omar Artan grateful for Super Cup chance after World Cup exclusion
news.lede: Referee was refused entry to US in June. Will take charge of PSG v Aston Villa on Wednesday. The Somali referee Omar Artan, who was refused entry to the US to officiate at the World Cup, has spoken publicly for the first time about the decision and detailed his pride as he prepares to take charge of the Super Cup match between Paris Saint‑Germain and Aston Villa on Wednesday. Uefa awarded the 34-year-old Artan the game a few days after he was prevented from working at the tournament.

news.title: Shaibu Urges Super Falcons To Keep World Cup Dream Alive
news.lede: Director General and Chief Executive Officer of the National Institute for Sports (NIS), Comrade Philip Shaibu, has urged the Super Falcons to remain focused on securing a place at the 2027 FIFA Women’s World Cup despite their elimination from the 2026 Women’s Africa Cup of Nations in Morocco. Nigeria’s hopes of defending their continental title were ended by Cameroon, but Shaibu believes the Super Falcons still have an opportunity to redeem themselves when they face South Africa in the World Cup qualification playoff on Thursday, August 13, 2026. The decisive encounter is scheduled to take place at the Moulay Rachid Stadium in Casablanca, with Shaibu urging the players to draw inspiration from Nigeria’s impressive record in African women’s football. “Super Falcons remain the most successful women’s team on the continent, having won the African title a record 10 times.
